stories.headline: IMD says a Bay of Bengal low may become a cyclonic storm by Monday evening
stories.summary: A well-marked low over the southeast Bay of Bengal is likely to become a depression within 24 hours and could strengthen into a cyclonic storm over the central Bay around Monday evening, the weather office said. Heavy rain is forecast for the Andaman and Nicobar Islands until Monday, and fishermen are told to stay away from the Andaman Sea. Delhi's air quality stayed 'very poor', with an AQI of 367 on Saturday evening.
stories.why_it_matters: A cyclone could disrupt shipping, fishing and crops along India's east coast later in the week.
stories.note: Single source: All India Radio (citing IMD).

stories.headline: Jaishankar says India-US trade deal should close soon once a few issues are settled
stories.summary: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar told a summit in New Delhi that the India-US trade deal should be concluded soon and must be fair to both sides. He said India's own interest will guide its response to the wars in Ukraine and the Gulf, and that states are now far more willing to take risks.
stories.why_it_matters: A US trade deal would cut tariff uncertainty for Indian exporters.

stories.headline: AIIMS Delhi does India's first open surgery on an unborn baby's spine
stories.summary: A team of more than 30 AIIMS doctors and nurses repaired a severe spina bifida defect in a 25-week fetus in a six-hour operation on November 12. The family paid nothing under a government maternity scheme. Mother and baby will be watched through birth.

stories.headline: Update: Iran's navy says two more tankers hit mines in Hormuz, seven in 24 hours
stories.summary: Iran's navy now says two more tankers struck naval mines and caught fire in the eastern Strait of Hormuz, which it counts as the seventh such incident in 24 hours, up from five in its earlier claim. Saudi-led coalition forces also say they shot down two Houthi drones. No ship names or independent proof have been given.
stories.why_it_matters: More ship hits in Hormuz could lift oil prices when markets reopen, raising India's import bill.
stories.note: Claims by Iran's navy and the Saudi-led coalition; not independently confirmed.

impact.why: Repeated reports of tankers hit in Hormuz add to supply risk for crude.

stories.headline: Hamas says Israeli drone strike killed its Rafah brigade commander in Gaza
stories.summary: Israel's military and Shin Bet say they hit a senior Hamas commander in a drone strike in Khan Younis on Saturday, and Hamas confirmed Samir Abu Younis was killed. The strike hit a tent for displaced people in al-Mawasi and wounded two others. Gaza's health ministry says 16 people were killed in the past 48 hours despite the ceasefire.
stories.note: Single source: Al Jazeera. Israel and Hamas both confirm the strike.

stories.headline: US envoy Kushner says he wants Europe and Russia to talk directly on Ukraine
stories.summary: Jared Kushner said on Saturday he is working with Russia, Ukraine and Europe to move peace talks to the next stage, including direct Europe-Moscow contact, and that both sides know compromises are needed. France's Macron said Europe must state clearly what it wants after the war. The Kremlin has said it is open to talks with Europe.

stories.headline: Italy fines Meta 805 million euros over Facebook app's access to users' photos
stories.summary: Italy's privacy regulator, the Garante, said the Facebook Android app reached users' photos and videos without specific consent, with a photo-suggestion feature switched on by default. It is the regulator's largest fine, about 0.47% of Meta's global turnover, and Meta must fix the consent notice. Meta can appeal.

impact.why: A record Italian privacy fine adds to Meta's regulatory costs in Europe.

stories.headline: More than 100,000 march across France against living costs; strike set for Tuesday
stories.summary: France's interior ministry counted 106,000 protesters nationwide on Saturday, down from 146,000 a week earlier; student unions said 200,000. Police used tear gas in Marseille, Lyon, Nantes, Bordeaux and Paris. Unions rejected a 0.6% minimum wage rise and called a new strike day for Tuesday.

stories.headline: Update: SpaceX catches a Starship upper stage with its tower for the first time
stories.summary: New since Friday's launch: the Starship upper stage came back from orbit on Saturday after about 22 hours and 14 laps of Earth and was caught by the tower's arms at Starbase, Texas. It had released 26 Starlink satellites. The planned double catch failed because the booster exploded on its way down on Friday, and engineers are investigating.
stories.why_it_matters: Catching the ship proves a fully reusable rocket can work, which could sharply cut the cost of reaching space.

image.alt: Starship rises beside its launch tower at Starbase, Texas, as spectators watch from a boat
